the-registry-and-retained-identity-outpu.text: The registry and retained identity outputs.

As an identity owner, I keep my checkpoint alive — bonds, rotations, unfreezing — until it is convicted; there is no owner exit, no parking and no revival. As a relying party, I see a checkpoint that is either alive or convicted, and I must refuse a termination-pending output. As a folder, I can process an admitted request without becoming the identity's controller.

These are model guarantees under their stated premises. The simulators execute model transactions; they do not establish Aiken, builder or deployed conformance. The no owner exit revision and the correspondence register own the lifecycle revision; the earlier parking revision is superseded. The earlier design record remains historical; its replaced lifecycle and economic claims are not current guarantees.

where-the-registry-is-built.text: The model imports the public Singular commit d69ab005c3b710aeebf033d3c5cd08c56feb5643, tree 2979dcfc58b092313b0ce7fa0493722539b9ea65, under Lean 4.27.0. The pinned sources define the imported generic booking, economic fold and rejection judgments. KERI owns its request lifecycle: until a request's deadline only a fold spends it; from the deadline anyone returns it through Registry.returnRequests, which refines the imported rejection with the deadline, registration-only and balance guards. The KERI registry is deployed with retractTime = 0, so no retraction window exists. Public upstream requirements include registration, termination, reading and integration. The executable model pin and those product requirements are distinct evidence.

Registry.Sys.toWorld projects KERI carriers and pending entries to the imported Singular.World. Registration booking and termination booking invoke its actual judgments. Registry.fold invokes Singular.foldAccepted, then reconstructs the KERI state and checks that its projection equals the returned world. RegistryAgreement.lean binds this correspondence. KERI retains its own admission, authorization, custody metadata and addressed local flows.

the-machine-registrylean.text: Sys contains the generation, imported configuration and trie, carriers, registration bookings, complete termination entries, treasury, permanent AID/token bindings and next token counter. A carrier stores its original holding, AID, token, key counter, local state and minimum ADA. A termination entry retains the complete generic booking and the original carrier metadata.

The coarse Registry predicates are inception and duplicity. They are declared abstractions, not cryptographic verification or a proof that they equal Checkpoint's concrete evidence predicates. In particular, the Registry flow does not summarize the Checkpoint conviction's bond and pool distribution.

Carrier.original is the stable imported holding descriptor retained as provenance. It does not prove equality with the complete serialized, evolving Checkpoint datum or a current ledger output reference. The separate coarse key counter and concrete Checkpoint key-state encoding are not universally equated by this adapter.

what-registration-guarantees.text: Given a reachable Registry state, the model preserves unique carrier and pending custody, permanent bindings and the imported world's invariant. A second successful first-registration cannot replace an active or retired key. There is no park and no revival, so no local step mints a new incarnation. These guarantees are scoped to one model registry.

RegistryReach.lean proves reachable well-formedness. RegistryCustody.lean and RegistryBurns.lean prove custody and the fold-only retirement boundary. RegistryMetadata.lean, RegistryFold.lean and RegistryCompleteness.lean prove reconstruction and completeness under the complete premises. RegistryAuthorization.lean proves the local authorization consequences. The numbered public consequences and inversions remain in RegistryGoals.lean.

An active key is not a consumer authorization. The reader must inspect the application output and enforce the consumer contract. Exact token bytes, canonical registry selection and transaction validity extensions remain in consumer authentication.

checkpoint-and-the-associated-system.text: Checkpoint.lean owns the funded local lifecycle: concrete duplicity, rotation and signed intent, conviction/freeze bonds, pool, refund address, poison, freeze and juvenility. There is no close and no reopen: a checkpoint leaves the live states only by conviction. The proved consumableStateB mirror refuses pending and convicted states.

SysStep adds the actual registered origin and pending request association. CheckpointCertificate.lean replays Registry history under the stored parameters, environment and initial configuration. Registration requires an actual accepted registration. Booking binds the request reference, AID, token, key state and complete entry to the origin. Completion needs an accepted fold consuming that exact entry. A valid receipt for a different request in the same context is insufficient. A local pending state has no local exit.

CheckpointCompletionGoals.lean states these receipt consequences. CheckpointSystemFixtures.lean supplies connected registration, rotation, conviction, booking and completion journeys, including a mixed fold and other-request refusals. The page's associated-system panel shows both addressed Checkpoint flow and Registry flow beside their full states.

booking-and-fold-economics.text: Given Mr + tip ≤ Mc, booking splits the carrier minimum ADA exactly:
Mr + tip funds the termination request.
Mc - Mr - tip is the booker's premium.
The booking fee is paid separately by the booker.

A live carrier retains Mc; it cannot pay that value to a reaper. Booking needs conviction first. Samaritan.booker_nonloss_iff compares the premium with the booking fee. There is no unconditional promise that a booker makes a profit.

The imported fold accounts for actual inputs, outputs, fees and donation. Registration delivers the declared carrier ADA, destination and datum to the token-bearing output and routes registration cost to treasury. Termination creates no carrier output: request ADA less declared tip goes to treasury, which is Mr for a matching KERI booking. Declared tips are ordinary value subject to transaction accounting, not an automatic payment to a named person. termination_fold_accounting and self_fold_addressed_accounting use those values. The latter requires all ordinary outputs at the named address, matching booking data and its other explicit transaction premises. A fold does not promise an automatic refund of Mr to the booker. Booking conservation and addressed self-fold accounting are different claims.

keris-application-on-the-public-registry.text: KERI's application on the public registry.

As a KERI registration requester, I book a request that the public Singular registry singular_state(A_keri) can fold into my checkpoint, and I know in advance what the fold or a later return does with my money and where my checkpoint will live. The public registry checks only that each folded request carries the registration approval its holding commits to, and that the holding holds at least the committed deposit. Everything else is KERI's application, stated in lean/CardanoKeri/Application.lean against the public model models/singular-application-held at the pin above. The Lean revision, the pin, the compiler and the script hashes and sizes of this generation are on the identities of this generation.

The application address holds only configuration records and requests. A delivered checkpoint lives at the checkpoint validator's own address, where its lifecycle (advance, conviction, freeze, top-up) spends it as the checkpoint and economic models state; the application never spends it. The one exception is the pending output a conviction leaves there: only a termination booking releases it, as the next section shows.

The configuration record. Each registry's genesis transaction mints one configuration record at the application address, holding the registration cost, minimum tip, processing time, booking width, retractTime = 0 and the credential of the checkpoint validator. A registry whose state policy is not state(A_keri) gets none (configuration_refuses_foreign_registry, configuration_refuses_retraction).

Booking. The booking reads the record by reference and mints exactly one registration approval. The approval commits the registry, the AID's key, the checkpoint validator's credential from the record as the holding address (never the application address), the hash of the initial checkpoint datum and the deposit, which is the whole carrier the checkpoint will hold: at least the minimum ADA plus the registry's deposit. The request holds exactly the deposit, the registration cost and the minimum tip (booking_inversion, booking_refuses_foreign_registry, booking_refuses_application_holding, booking_refuses_other_holding, booking_refuses_short_deposit, booking_refuses_inexact_contents).

Spending a request. Until its deadline, the booking's validity upper bound plus the processing time, a request is spent only by a fold that delivers the committed holding: at the checkpoint validator's credential the record names, with the committed initial datum, exactly the deposit and the one new active token. From the deadline anyone may return it, paying the refund address everything but the tip (registration_spend_is_fold_or_return, before_deadline_only_fold, fold_delivers_to_checkpoint_validator, return_pays_refund_address, fold_refuses_inexact_holding). With retractTime = 0 the two windows are the public model's processing and cleanup phases (windows_are_upstream_phases).

The initial checkpoint state. The delivered holding's datum is exactly the state the checkpoint model's registration step writes for the request: the version 2 Live datum of the AID whose key the request names, at sequence number and epoch 0, neither poisoned, frozen nor topped up, born at the booking's validity upper bound and refunding to the ledger bytes of the refund address the request names; its pool, the deposit less the minimum ADA, the checkpoint deposit and the freeze bond, covers at least one premium. A fold delivering any other sequence number, epoch, flag, birth slot, refund address, AID or a pending termination, or a pool below one premium, is refused, so no fold can deliver a checkpoint that skips the juvenility window or claims a key state the KEL never reached (fold_delivers_initial_state, delivered_initial_state, initialState_is_registration, fold_refuses_other_state, fold_refuses_other_aid, fold_refuses_pool_below_premium, fold_refuses_unrecorded_refund). The key material in the datum is pinned by the committed datum hash, not by this rule. One transaction folds at most one registration request in the on-chain realization; that is a declared limit of the realization, not of the model.

A genuine checkpoint. What a fold delivers for a booked request is a genuine checkpoint: at the checkpoint validator, not the application address; holding the one active token of the AID's key under a registry of state(A_keri); carrying the version 2 datum the request committed; holding exactly the deposit (delivered_is_genuine, before_deadline_delivers_genuine, genuine_holds_committed_datum). A consumer whose context names the same checkpoint credential, registry and AID accepts it exactly when the written state is consumable (genuine_checkpoint_consumable_iff). No input the application spends at its own address is a checkpoint (no_application_input_is_a_checkpoint).

The closed mint. Everything a transaction mints or burns under the application policy is exactly what its actions justify: one configuration token per created record, one registration approval per booked output, one termination approval per termination booking, one approval burned per fold or return, one termination approval burned per terminating fold. Each booked output is booked once. An approval minted without a booking, a second booking of one output, or any other token under the application policy is refused (accepted_mint_is_justified, accepted_books_once, mint_without_booking_refused, duplicate_booking_refused).

The treasury. A fold's ledger treasury_donation is at least the registration costs of the registration requests it folds and, for each termination request it folds, the request's lovelace less the minimum tip (treasury_covers_registration_costs, folded_cost_in_donation, termination_fold_donates). The tip is what the folder may keep.

Termination custody. A termination request has no deadline and is spent only by a fold that reads the configuration record by reference and burns its termination approval and its active token while the state policy runs (termination_only_by_fold).

retiring-a-convicted-identity.text: As a relying party, I want an identity convicted under KERI's duplicity rule to become permanently terminal in its registry, so that no checkpoint for its key can ever be served again, and I want nobody to be able to end an identity that was not convicted. As anyone watching the chain, I can carry a conviction through to the registry myself, without anyone's signature, and keep what the booking frees as my premium.

Retirement takes three transactions. A conviction, on the checkpoint validator, pays the convictor and the refund address and leaves a pending output at the checkpoint validator's address: a pending-termination datum, exactly the registry's minimum ADA and the registry's active token. A termination booking, open to anyone, spends that pending output, mints exactly one termination approval of the registry and of the key of the datum's AID, and places the termination request at the application address with an empty datum, exactly the active token and the approval, holding the economic termination carrier plus the registry's minimum tip. The booker keeps the rest of the minimum ADA, which is the economic booking premium. A terminating fold then spends the request, burns the approval and the active token, donates the request less the tip to the treasury, and the public registry makes the key terminal.
The guarantees, each a theorem of lean/CardanoKeri/ApplicationGoals.lean:

No termination without a conviction. A termination approval is minted only by a booking of exactly that registry and key, which spends, once, an output at the checkpoint validator holding exactly the minimum ADA and the key's one active token and carrying the pending-termination datum of an AID whose key it is; exactly one approval is minted. Where the checkpoint validator realizes the checkpoint model, that output's checkpoint was convicted, with duplicity evidence at its last key state (termination_approval_requires_booking, termination_approval_requires_pending, termination_approval_requires_conviction, and in the checkpoint model pending_only_by_conviction and reachable_pending_convicted).

The checkpoint validator releases a pending output only into a booking. Its one spend of a pending output requires exactly one termination approval of its key to be minted, which the application mints only in a booking (pending_released_only_into_booking).
The request is what the fold consumes. The booking places exactly the output the terminating fold accepts, holding the economic carrier plus the minimum tip (termination_booking_inversion).

The money is the economic model's. The request holds what the economic booking puts into the request and the booker keeps the economic premium (termination_booking_matches_reap); the fold's donation is the economic termination donation, the carrier (termination_donation_matches_economic).

The key retires for good. A terminating fold that is a step of the public registry's history makes the key terminal (termination_fold_retires_key); no later transaction, whatever it is, makes it anything else or mints its active token (terminal_key_permanent). A termination booking of a terminal key is refused, because no unspent output holds its active token (termination_booking_refused_for_terminal_key), and a fold registering it again is refused, because the registry's insertion requires an unknown key and mints no active token for a terminal one (registration_fold_refused_for_terminal_key).
The registry key stays active from the conviction through the booking: the pending output and then the request hold its one active token. Only the terminating fold retires it.

Two approvals that are the same token name the same deployment, registry seed, AID, holding address, initial datum hash and deposit, under the finite encoding and collision-freedom premises of the identity bytes (approval_binds). The network is not in any approval: a Plutus address carries no network identifier. It is fixed by the chain the transaction runs on, where the ledger refuses outputs naming another network and the registry seed exists on one chain only (approval_ignores_network); this is a declared boundary of the model. The request lovelace and the return's refund are the economic model's declared contents and refund floor when the economic tip is the minimum tip and the carrier is the deposit (request_matches_economic, carrier_floor_matches_economic); the economic model stays the authority for the registry, custody and termination theorems above.

lean/application-vectors.json, printed by lean/ApplicationDriver.lean, gives the approval bytes, the configuration record with its checkpoint validator credential, and accepted and refused configuration creations, bookings, folds, returns, termination spends and spends of a delivered checkpoint for the on-chain approval and checkpoint creation (#348). For the retirement of a convicted identity (#350) it adds the termination approval bytes, accepted and refused termination bookings and terminating folds, and the checkpoint validator's release verdicts. The request and configuration datums' own byte layouts are not fixed by these vectors.

executable-evidence-and-limits.text: The Registry simulator replays complete wire-v3 transactions, including refusals and economic boundaries. The Checkpoint simulator has local lifecycle stories and a separate associated-system player. The canonical reader stories are simulator/M1-STORIES.md and simulator/REGISTRY-STORIES.md.

The Lean build, exact contract checks, compiled axiom inventory, finite model mutations, fresh corpus replay and browser/CLI checks cover separate evidence classes. Their source bindings are recorded with the candidate. Finite examples are not the universal proofs; checker mutations are not model mutations.

The model does not establish production transaction construction, submission, rollback handling, live-chain availability or cryptographic codec correctness. Broader application request recovery remains in request lifecycle. Those obligations require their own model correspondence and both implementation test layers before production acceptance.
